claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.label: Apical-in spheroids become motile within a week in low-adhesive liquid culture
claims.statement: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids that are apical-in and non-motile on release from Matrigel become motile by day 7 in low-adhesive liquid culture, with beating cilia on their outer surface; immunostaining shows a large increase in external multiciliated cells between day 0 and day 7.

operationalizations.text: Compare day-0 and day-7 displacement, surface-cilia video, and external multiciliated-cell staining in the same protocol cohort.

Score the fraction of apical-in spheroids that translocate on day 0 and on day 7 after release into low-adhesive liquid culture, and count external multiciliated cells by acetylated-tubulin staining at the same times. A rise in both motility and external cilia would support the time course; motility without external cilia, or no change by day 7, would refute it.

obstacles: Not all spheroids may be represented in public media.
Different specimens may supply day-0 and day-7 staining.
Motility counts and cilia tallies are in figures and are not a deposited table.
Day-7 staining is a separate sample from the tracked spheroids, so the pairing is by cohort rather than by individual.
The public videos are examples, not the every-other-day census.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central: Motile Living Biobots supporting materials
roles: open day-specific images, videos, measurements, and protocol

claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Morphogenetic control as a collective intelligence
claims.label: Tadpoles see through an ectopic tail eye without generations of adaptation
claims.statement: Tadpoles whose native eyes are prevented from forming and which carry an ectopic eye on the tail can see and perform well in visual behavioural training even though that eye connects to the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain, so a radical change to sensory–motor architecture yields successful behaviour without generations of adaptation.

operationalizations.text: Compare blinded visual-learning performance of eyeless tadpoles with tail eyes, eyeless controls, and normal-eye controls, stratified by whether the graft innervates spinal cord or peripheral tissue. Above-control acquisition and transfer would confirm vision through the ectopic eye.

Score visual learning in Xenopus tadpoles with native eyes prevented and one ectopic eye on the tail, and record whether that eye's axons enter the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain. Learning above the no-eye and extraocular-photoreception controls would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that survives removal of the ectopic eye, would refute it.

obstacles: Animal-level trial data and innervation classifications may not be public.
Light-mediated nonvisual cues require controls.
Performance does not identify the adaptive neural mechanism.
Extraocular light sensitivity can imitate vision unless the ectopic eye is covered or removed as a control.
The behavioural trials are published as summary performance, not as a public trial table.

claims.label: Altering planarian voltage patterns changes head number and head species-shape
claims.statement: In planaria, manipulating the endogenous bioelectric voltage pattern by targeting gap junctions or ion channels can produce worms with one, two or zero heads, or with head and brain shapes resembling other extant planarian species.

operationalizations.text: Compare head count, head outline, brain morphology, and voltage maps after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation with vehicle controls and reference species using blinded image classification.

Count heads, and compare head and brain landmarks to reference species, after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation versus vehicle; the claim holds if one, two, and zero heads, and non-native head shapes, occur above the vehicle rate.

obstacles: Raw images and voltage measurements may be incomplete.
Drug treatments can have off-target effects.
Resemblance to another species depends on the morphometric classifier.
Most quantitative series come from one laboratory, and raw images are not in a measurement archive.
Planform encodes published outcomes and may omit landmark-level shapes from later papers.
Toxicity can change head number unless vehicle and washout controls are carried along.

claims.label: Two-headed planarian state persists through further cutting despite wild-type genome
claims.statement: Planaria with abnormal head number induced by transient bioelectric manipulation are permanently altered: when cut into pieces with no further treatment, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number despite wild-type genetics.

operationalizations.text: Track head number across serial amputations after transient treatment has ended, compare with vehicle controls, and verify unchanged genotype; persistence across untreated rounds supports a stable non-genetic state.

Cut transiently treated two-headed or zero-headed worms with no further drug and score head number in successive regenerates, alongside a wild-type sequence or drug-residue assay; persistence holds if abnormal head number continues after the drug is gone and the genome matches wild type.

obstacles: Complete worm-level lineage records may not be public.
Residual treatment or stable tissue changes must be excluded.
Permanence is bounded by the observed regeneration rounds.
Penetrance tables are in the papers, not as animal-level files.
Residual drug or a selected genetic variant can mimic a permanent physiological state.
Wild-type genome is argued from induction and reset experiments more often than from deposited sequence of the altered lines.

claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue
claims.label: Bioelectric network information cannot be read from transcript or protein levels
claims.statement: Because ion channels open and close post-translationally, the same channels can yield different voltage states depending on cell history and different channels can yield the same voltage map, the information content of a bioelectric network cannot be read out at the transcriptional or proteomic level and must be studied in living tissue.

operationalizations.text: Train models to predict live voltage maps from matched transcriptomic or proteomic profiles across tissues and histories, and test identifiability on held-out samples. Demonstrating the same molecular profile with different voltages and different profiles with the same voltage would refute a unique readout.

In paired transcriptome and electrophysiology profiles, predict resting or firing features from transcript levels and ask whether distinct channel sets map to the same electrical phenotype. Prediction no better than a permutation null, or identical transcriptomes with different voltage states, would support unreadability; accurate prediction of the electrical phenotype from transcripts or proteins would refute a strict reading.

obstacles: Matched live voltage and omics measurements are uncommon.
Bulk omics obscures cell-level states.
Failure of prediction can reflect measurement limits rather than impossibility.
The atlas covers spiking neurons, not the slow developmental voltage patterns the surrounding argument is about.
A snapshot cannot test history dependence, and proteins are not paired with voltage in this resource.

roles: public patch-seq and electrophysiology for mammalian cortical neurons, pairing transcripts with electrical features

claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Non-neural Bioelectricity: What Bodies Think About
claims.label: Voltage-sensitive channels and gap junctions form rewritable dynamical memories
claims.statement: Because ion channels and gap junctions are themselves voltage-sensitive, a transient voltage state can trigger progressive depolarization or gap-junction closure, so non-neural bioelectric circuits readily form dynamical-system memories that store information and change computation without changing the channel or junction hardware.

operationalizations.text: Construct or reuse conductance models with voltage-sensitive channels and junctions, apply transient inputs, and test for multiple persistent attractors and altered input-output behavior with unchanged parameters.

Simulate a transient voltage pulse with published channel and connexin gating and test for two stable voltages or coupling states; dynamical memory holds if the post-pulse state remains after the pulse and changes later input-output behavior with the same hardware.

obstacles: Model attractors do not show that living non-neural tissues use them as memory.
Biophysical parameters for many non-neural networks are sparse.
Most kinetic parameters come from neurons or heterologous cells, not the non-neural tissues in the claim.
A persistent voltage in real tissue can be transcriptional or ultrastructural rather than a dynamical-system memory of the same channels.

claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales
claims.label: Bioelectrically induced two-headed planaria stay two-headed across later regenerations
claims.statement: In planarian flatworms the number of heads a regenerating fragment builds is set by the state of a bioelectric circuit with a default of one; transiently modifying it re-sets it to 'two', and the resulting two-headed worms keep regenerating as two-headed through multiple rounds of cutting without further manipulation, unless the pattern is experimentally reset.

operationalizations.text: Track treated founders and all fragments through multiple untreated cuts, recording head number and bioelectric state, with sham-treated and reset-to-one controls. Stable two-headed regeneration across lineages, reversed by a targeted bioelectric reset, confirms persistent physiological inheritance.

After a transient bioelectric or gap-junction treatment, cut fragments in later rounds with no further drug and record head number, plus a reset cohort returned to one head by a second manipulation. Two-headed regenerates across rounds, reversed by the reset and not by washout alone, would support a stored target; return to one head as soon as the drug is gone, or a heritable mutation, would refute it.

obstacles: Raw lineage data may not be deposited.
Persistent drug, microbiome, or epigenetic effects are alternative carriers.
Permanent is bounded by the number of observed rounds.
Round-by-round head counts are in the experimental papers, not a deposited lineage table.
A persistent non-genetic store other than the bioelectric circuit, including bacteria, can keep the two-headed outcome.

claims.label: Tadpoles with eyes on their tails can still perform visual learning
claims.statement: Xenopus tadpoles engineered to have eyes on their tails instead of their heads are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks, illustrating that minds readily adapt to radically altered body architectures.

operationalizations.text: Compare acquisition and retention of a visual discrimination task among tadpoles with tail eyes, sham surgery, native eyes, and no functional eyes, using blinded trial-level choice data.

In the light-mediated learning assay, compare choice performance of tadpoles with ectopic tail eyes and native eyes removed against blind and normal-eyed animals; visual learning holds if only animals with a functional eye-brain path exceed chance.

obstacles: Complete trial-level records may not be openly available.
The broad conclusion about minds adapting exceeds the specific visual-learning assay.
Trial-level choice logs are in the papers' summaries, not a public repository.
Both positive reports come from the same group, so an independent replicate is not in the open record.

claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion
claims.label: Bioelectric circuits act as software: multistable states switched without genetic change
claims.statement: Ion channel and gap junction circuits are well suited to the "software" of life because they form feedback loops that implement dynamical systems with multiple attractors, which transient signals can switch between without changing the hardware (i.e. without mutating the DNA encoding the channels).

operationalizations.text: Construct or reuse ion-channel and gap-junction dynamical models, identify multiple stable physiological attractors, and demonstrate switching by transient inputs while parameters representing channel-encoding DNA remain fixed.

In an ion-channel and gap-junction network, show at least two stable Vmem patterns and a transient stimulus that switches them with channel genes held fixed. Multistability under fixed parameters would support the software analogy in the model; a unique steady state, or a switch that requires changing channel expression, would refute it there. The tissue reading additionally needs a transient in vivo stimulus that permanently changes anatomy without a DNA change.

obstacles: Existence in selected circuits does not show all bioelectric networks are multistable.
Software is a metaphor beyond the stated dynamical properties.
A multistable model does not show that tissues occupy those attractors.
Transcriptional memory can store a new anatomical state with the DNA sequence unchanged.
No public time series records an in vivo bioelectric switch and the subsequent attractor.

claims.work: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Introduction
claims.label: Planaria have chaotic genomes yet regenerate, resist cancer and do not age
claims.statement: Planaria, despite chaotic mixoploid genomes from ~400 million years of asexual reproduction and large numbers of plastic proliferative stem cells, are champions of regeneration, cancer resistant and apparently do not age, the opposite of what a 'genome drives function' paradigm would predict.

operationalizations.text: Quantify planarian somatic ploidy and genomic heterogeneity, regeneration success, neoplasm incidence and age-related functional decline, and compare them with preregistered taxa and genome-instability predictions. The descriptive conjunction is supported if high instability coexists with exceptional repair and low senescence and cancer.

From public assemblies, measure heterozygosity, repeats, and ploidy variation in asexual Schmidtea, and compile regeneration success, tumor incidence under defined challenges, and survival curves. High genomic disorder together with high regeneration, low tumor incidence, and no actuarial aging would support the generalization; a stable diploid genome, poor regeneration, or a clear aging curve in the asexual strain would refute the corresponding clause.

obstacles: Apparently do not age is stronger than available lifespan evidence.
Cancer incidence in wild and laboratory planaria is poorly sampled.
The paradigm prediction is not quantitatively specified.
Lifespan and tumor-incidence numbers are not in the genome databases and are sparse for asexual strains.
Sexual Schmidtea aging data do not directly cover the asexual animals named in the claim.
Champions of regeneration is a comparative ranking without a single coded trait matrix.

claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation
claims.label: Ion channel drugs can make planarian head number flip stochastically at each regeneration
claims.statement: Exposure to ion channel drugs can put the planarian bioelectric circuit into a bistable state in which, at each regeneration, fragments of these 'cryptic' worms randomly regenerate as one-headed or two-headed, analogous to bistability in perceptual systems.

operationalizations.text: Track identified treated worms and their fragments over repeated regeneration rounds, estimate transition probabilities between one- and two-head outcomes, and compare them with fixed-state and untreated controls. A reproducible nonzero switching process without further drug exposure confirms bistable or stochastic phenotype switching.

For fragments from ion-channel-drug-treated cryptic worms, record head number at each successive regeneration without further drug and test whether the two outcomes occur as draws rather than as a fixed lineage state. Frequencies near a stable mixture, with individual lines flipping, would support bistable recall; each fragment locking to one morphology, or flipping only while the drug remains, would refute it.

obstacles: Raw longitudinal lineage records may not be public.
Apparent randomness may reflect unmeasured physiological state.
Stochastic switching does not uniquely establish circuit bistability.
Per-fragment outcome sequences are not a public table, so published proportions could hide stable subclasses.
Environmental noise between cuts can imitate a bistable circuit.
